purpose: Isolate the effect of inverse source/class frequency weighting on development FP and individual spam detection retention
campaign_policy: Separate experimental fork with its own lineage metadata, artifacts and budget; do not modify or impersonate the monthly campaign

arms.control: Existing inverse source/class frequency weights and ham_cost=2
arms.candidate: Remove inverse source/class frequency factors; keep ham_cost=2 and global mean normalization

controls: same verified parent adapters, AdamW, scheduler and RNG
same first 500 continuation steps and TRAIN row order
same batch size, tokenizer, max_length, backbone, rank, learning rate and CPU environment
each fork records verified parent metadata plus its own explicit changed objective; do not bypass monthly metadata checks

evaluation.partition: Frozen SELECT only; development, not independent
report: FP/FN, log loss, fixed 0.5 threshold and separately fitted development ~98% threshold
per-identity lost/gained TP and removed/added FP versus both parent and control
evaluation.do_not_infer: Equal aggregate TP is not zero loss of prior individual detections

acceptance: No product promotion from this ablation. Later v80 per-identity no-loss plus FP decrease and independent evaluation remain required
